title: The Marvel Comics Vault
intro: [whispers] Welcome to Disney Jeopardy, and welcome to the vault. Tonight we open the oldest long boxes in the House of Ideas, from the 1930s to the Disney deal. [chuckles] White gloves only, superfans.

art.prompt: A dim archive vault with tall metal shelves of protective comic boxes, a single reading lamp and a velvet rope, original painterly animated-film style artwork, wide 16:9 composition, no text, no logos, no recognizable copyrighted characters.

categories.title: Timely Beginnings
categories.intro: We begin before the Marvel name, in the golden age of comics. [warmly] Grab your fedora.

art.prompt: A bustling 1940s publishing office with drafting tables, ink bottles and a city skyline in the window, original painterly animated-film style artwork, wide 16:9 composition, no text, no logos, no recognizable copyrighted characters.

clues.clue: Marvel's publisher launched its first comics in 1939 under this company name.
clues.reveal: [excited] The correct answer is Timely Comics! Where it all started.

clues.clue: Marvel Comics #1 introduced the android Human Torch and this hot-tempered undersea prince.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Namor the Sub-Mariner! [chuckles] Ankle wings since 1939.

clues.clue: Captain America Comics #1 famously shows Cap punching this dictator on the cover, months before the U.S. entered the war.
clues.reveal: [excited] The correct answer is Hitler! A bold cover from March 1941.

clues.clue: Captain America was created by Joe Simon and this legendary artist.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Jack Kirby! [excited] The King of comics.

clues.clue: In the 1950s, before taking the Marvel name, the company published as this.
clues.reveal: [excited] The correct answer is Atlas Comics! Monsters, westerns, and a globe logo.

categories.title: Silver Age Debuts
categories.intro: The early sixties, when heroes popped up in anthology comics. [excited] Name the issue, the year or the title.

art.prompt: A spinner rack of colorful 1960s comic books in a corner drugstore, no readable text, original painterly animated-film style artwork, wide 16:9 composition, no text, no logos, no recognizable copyrighted characters.

clues.clue: The Incredible Hulk #1 smashed onto newsstands in this year.
clues.reveal: [excited] The correct answer is 1962! He was gray at first, by the way.

clues.clue: Iron Man debuted in 1963 in this anthology series.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Tales of Suspense! [excited] Issue 39.

clues.clue: Hank Pym first shrank in the pages of this anthology series.
clues.reveal: [chuckles] The correct answer is Tales to Astonish! Small hero, big title.

clues.clue: Doctor Strange made his debut in 1963 in this fittingly named anthology.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Strange Tales! [dramatically] Issue 110, by Lee and Ditko.

clues.clue: The Avengers #1 and The X-Men #1 share this cover-date month and year.
clues.reveal: [excited] The correct answer is September 1963! Two teams, one magical month.

categories.title: Bullpen Bulletins
categories.intro: Our fan category: the people and phrases behind the House of Ideas. [chuckles] Make mine Marvel.

art.prompt: A cluttered 1960s office bullpen with drafting tables in rows, full of sketches, original painterly animated-film style artwork, wide 16:9 composition, no text, no logos, no recognizable copyrighted characters.

clues.clue: Stan Lee famously signed off his columns with this one-word cheer.
clues.reveal: [excited] The correct answer is Excelsior! Upward and onward, true believers.

clues.clue: Stan's columns called Marvel's staff of writers and artists this.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is the Bullpen! [chuckles] Rascally, merry and very busy.

clues.clue: In this production style, artists drew from a plot outline and the writer added dialogue later.
clues.reveal: [excited] The correct answer is the Marvel Method! Fast, collaborative and still debated.

clues.clue: Marvel's official 1960s fan club had this alliterative name.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is the Merry Marvel Marching Society! [sings] Membership kit included a record.

clues.clue: Stan Lee was born with this name.
clues.reveal: [warmly] The correct answer is Stanley Lieber! Stan Lee was a pen name that stuck.

categories.title: Key Issue Gallery
categories.intro: Picture category! Each image is inspired by a key moment in early Marvel comics. Tell me what I'm asking for.

art.prompt: A museum gallery wall of empty gilded frames lit by spotlights, velvet benches in front, original painterly animated-film style artwork, wide 16:9 composition, no text, no logos, no recognizable copyrighted characters.

clues.clue: Marvel Comics #1 starred an android who did this. Name him. Pictured: a glowing humanoid figure made entirely of flames flying over a 1940s city skyline at night.
clues.reveal: [excited] The correct answer is the original Human Torch! An android, not Johnny Storm.

media.prompt: A glowing humanoid figure made entirely of flames flying over a 1940s city skyline at night, original painterly illustration, no text, no logos, no people, no recognizable copyrighted characters.

clues.clue: Bruce Banner was caught in the blast of this kind of bomb, shown here. Pictured: a desert test site with a huge glowing green blast cloud rising over the horizon and a small jeep in the foreground.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is a gamma bomb! [dramatically] He went to save a teenager. Hero move.

media.prompt: A desert test site with a huge glowing green blast cloud rising over the horizon and a small jeep in the foreground, original painterly illustration, no text, no logos, no people, no recognizable copyrighted characters.

clues.clue: Exposure to these during a rocket flight gave the Fantastic Four their powers. What were they? Pictured: a small 1960s style rocket ship flying through a storm of glowing colorful energy streaks in space.
clues.reveal: [excited] The correct answer is cosmic rays! Shielding? Never heard of it.

media.prompt: A small 1960s style rocket ship flying through a storm of glowing colorful energy streaks in space, original painterly illustration, no text, no logos, no people, no recognizable copyrighted characters.

clues.clue: Tony Stark's first armor, built in captivity, was this color in his 1963 debut. Pictured: a bulky clunky iron suit of armor with rivets standing in a dim cave workshop full of scrap metal.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is gray! [chuckles] The gold paint came next issue.

media.prompt: A bulky clunky iron suit of armor with rivets standing in a dim cave workshop full of scrap metal, original painterly illustration, no text, no logos, no people, no recognizable copyrighted characters.

clues.clue: In Thor's 1962 debut, Dr. Donald Blake transforms by striking this on the ground. What is it? Pictured: a gnarled old wooden walking stick lying on the floor of a dark Norwegian sea cave.
clues.reveal: [dramatically] The correct answer is a walking stick! He found it in a cave in Norway.

media.prompt: A gnarled old wooden walking stick lying on the floor of a dark Norwegian sea cave, glowing faintly, original painterly illustration, no text, no logos, no people, no recognizable copyrighted characters.

categories.title: House of Mouse Archive
categories.intro: To the parks archives: Marvel's road to Disney, and some early experiments. [whispers] Very deep cuts.

art.prompt: A dusty archive room with blueprints pinned up, scale models of park buildings and a desk lamp, original painterly animated-film style artwork, wide 16:9 composition, no text, no logos, no recognizable copyrighted characters.

clues.clue: Disney's deal to acquire Marvel Entertainment was announced in this year.
clues.reveal: [excited] The correct answer is 2009! The House of Mouse met the House of Ideas.

clues.clue: The Marvel deal was valued at roughly this much.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is about four billion dollars! [chuckles] Chet would have chipped in.

clues.clue: Before Avengers Campus, Disney California Adventure tested the waters with this 2017 Marvel seasonal event.
clues.reveal: [excited] The correct answer is Summer of Heroes! Guardians dance party included.

clues.clue: At Disneyland's old Innoventions building, guests could meet the god of thunder at this attraction.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Thor: Treasures of Asgard! [excited] Tomorrowland had a little Asgard.

clues.clue: Hong Kong Disneyland's Ant-Man and The Wasp: Nano Battle! replaced this attraction.
clues.reveal: [excited] The correct answer is Buzz Lightyear Astro Blasters! To infinity, and then very small.
